headline: Launch contracts soar. Small nations join. Space resilience funding increases.
deck: This week saw significant moves in launch contracts, international space agreements, and funding for space resilience.

stories.head: Space Force triples launch ceiling to $17 billion
stories.body: The Space Force has tripled its launch contract ceiling to $17 billion, responding to rising demand for satellite launches. This decision underscores the military's increasing reliance on commercial launch capabilities, which are now seen as essential to national security. Expect a flurry of bids as companies scramble to secure their piece of the pie.
stories.soWhat: This is a clear signal that the U.S. intends to leverage commercial capabilities more aggressively, which could squeeze smaller players out of the market.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid defense drive
stories.body: True Anomaly has secured $190 million in a Series C round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The funding highlights a strong demand for co-orbital security solutions and space domain awareness, as the DoD pushes for enhanced capabilities in these areas. Investors are clearly banking on the growing importance of space in defense strategies.
stories.soWhat: When defense budgets are tight, companies that can demonstrate a clear connection to national security will thrive, leaving less focused ventures in the dust.

stories.head: Mauritius signs Artemis Accords, joins space club
stories.body: Mauritius has become the 70th nation to sign the Artemis Accords, signaling a broader global interest in lunar exploration and collaboration. This move, while seemingly symbolic, reflects a growing recognition among smaller nations of the strategic importance of space. As the U.S. expands its partnerships, expect more countries to jump on the bandwagon.
stories.soWhat: The more nations that join the Artemis Accords, the more complex the geopolitical landscape becomes—space diplomacy is about to get a lot more crowded.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on SpaceX secondary market
watchlist.body: With SpaceX's valuation hitting $470 billion, the secondary market is likely to see increased activity as investors weigh their options.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris tactical bid developments
watchlist.body: Their collaboration for the tactical SDA constellation could reshape the competitive landscape in military satellite communications.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser progress

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
